title: The generic ordinary component count is a lower bound after shrinking
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $Y$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Suppose the scheme-theoretic generic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has exactly $n$ irreducible components, where $n\geq0$ is a finite integer. There is a nonempty open subset $V\subseteq Y$ such that $X_t$ has at least $n$ irreducible components for every $t\in V$. These are ordinary irreducible components over $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field], without passage to a field extension. No flatness, separatedness or Noetherian assumption on $f$ or $Y$ is imposed.

proof.text: If $n=0$, take $V=Y$: every fibre has at least zero components and $Y$ is nonempty because it has the generic point $\eta$. Hence assume $n>0$. Enumerate the distinct irreducible components of $X_\eta$ as $C_1,\ldots,C_n$. They are nonempty closed subsets by [def-weil-irreducible-components], and they cover $X_\eta$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover].

Identify $X_\eta$ with $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ using [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For each $i$, let $D_i$ be the closure in $X$ of the image of $C_i$, and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be its reduced induced closed subscheme, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. In the subspace $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$, the intersection with this closure is the closure of $C_i$ in that subspace, namely $C_i$. Consequently the underlying space of $(X_i)_\eta$ is $C_i$. More generally, write $D_{i,t}=D_i\cap f^{-1}(\{t\})$ as a closed subset of $X_t$ via the fibre homeomorphism. The fibre homeomorphisms for $f$ and $f\circ j_i$ identify $(X_i)_t$ with $D_{i,t}$, with its subspace topology.

source.place: Tag 0554, reduced closures of the generic components; discussion immediately before Tag 054Y (lemma-cover-generic-fibre-neighbourhood).

proof.text: Each $h_i=f\circ j_i:X_i\to Y$ is of finite type. Indeed, over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$, choose the finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ of $f^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with each $B_a$ generated by finitely many elements over $A$. The inverse images under $j_i$ are affine $\operatorname{Spec}(B_a/I_{i,a})$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. They form a finite cover, and the images of those same generators generate each quotient over $A$. This proves both local finite type and quasi-compactness, without requiring $I_{i,a}$ to be finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 0554, finite type of the reduced closed component closures, made explicit from the affine definitions.

proof.text: Fix $i\ne j$. Distinct maximal irreducible subsets $C_i,C_j$ cannot contain one another, so $C_i\cap C_j$ is a proper closed subset of the irreducible space $C_i$. Its complement is dense: every nonempty open of an irreducible space meets every other nonempty open, by the two-closed-set definition [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $W_{ij}=X_i\setminus j_i^{-1}(D_j)$, an open of $X_i$. By Step 2 its generic fibre is precisely that dense complement in $C_i$. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-open-fibre-density] to $h_i$, $W_{ij}$ and $\eta$. Step 3 gives finite type, and $\overline{\{\eta\}}=Y$. Obtain an open $U_{ij}\subseteq Y$ containing $\eta$ such that $D_{i,t}\setminus D_{j,t}$ is dense in $D_{i,t}$ for every $t\in U_{ij}$. This is exactly the nowhere-dense-intersection assertion used in the source, expressed by open complements.

source.place: Tag 0554, invocation of Tag 054X (lemma-nowhere-dense-generic-fibre) for the pairwise intersections.

proof.text: The finite union $D=\bigcup_{i=1}^nD_i$ is closed and contains $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ by Steps 1 and 2. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-fibre-closed-cover-spread] to $g=f$, $y=\eta$, $C=D$ and the second closed subset $\varnothing$. Its hypotheses are finite type of $f$ and the displayed generic covering. As $\overline{\{\eta\}}=Y$, it gives an open $U_0$ containing $\eta$ such that $X_t=\bigcup_iD_{i,t}$ for every $t\in U_0$, under the fibre homeomorphism [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Using a single finite union as its first closed set avoids any induction or assumption on the number of closed sets in the cited statement.

For each $i$, $D_i$ is a closed subset of $X$ meeting $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$, since $C_i$ is nonempty. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-closed-subset-fibre-nonempty] to $h=f$, $P=X$, $T=Y$, and this closed subset $D_i$. The theorem assumes exactly finite type and a generic point of the whole base, with no reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis. It gives an open $U_i$ containing $\eta$ such that $D_{i,t}$ is nonempty for every $t\in U_i$. This packages the generic-flatness and openness argument of the source into the existing nonemptiness tool.

By Step 2, each $D_{i,t}$ is the underlying space of the scheme fibre $(X_i)_t$, and each set $D_{i,t}\setminus D_{j,t}$ is open in $D_{i,t}$ because $D_{j,t}$ is closed. Step 4 says these finitely many open subsets are dense in $D_{i,t}$, while Step 6 says $D_{i,t}$ is nonempty. Apply [lem-trf-finite-dense-open-intersection], whose statement gives that the intersection of any finite family of dense open subsets of a topological space is dense, hence nonempty in this $D_{i,t}$. source.place: Tag 0554, final paragraph: nonempty closed covering pieces with nowhere-dense pairwise intersections.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], choose an irreducible component $K_i$ of $X_t$ containing $x_i$. The covering in Step 5 gives $K_i=\bigcup_{j=1}^n(K_i\cap D_{j,t})$, a finite closed covering of the irreducible space $K_i$. Repeatedly applying the two-closed-set definition of irreducibility [def-weil-irreducible-components] shows that $K_i$ is contained in one $D_{j,t}$. Since $x_i$ belongs to none of the other pieces, this index must be $i$. If $i\ne j$ and $K_i=K_j$, then $x_i\in K_j\subseteq D_{j,t}$, a contradiction. Hence $K_1,\ldots,K_n$ are distinct irreducible components of the ordinary fibre $X_t$. This proves the required lower bound. No field extension or geometric-component comparison has entered the argument.
